newsitem.title: USA: Genesis says may ask Imagex CEO to resign.
newsitem.headline: Genesis says may ask Imagex CEO to resign.

text.p: Genesis Insurance & Financial Service Inc, which recently acquired a majority stake in Imagex Services Inc, said it may seek the resignation of Imagex Chief Executive Andrew Cappocia and may seek Chapter 11 bankruptcy reorganization for Imagex.

Genesis Chief Executive Mohamed Khairy Mohamed Zayed said in a statement that when it acquired the stake in the company "some weeks ago, we have obtained very disturbing information which will more than likely result in our changing our original strategy with Imagex Services Inc."
Genesis declined to offer specific details about the information it had received since acquiring the company. Neither Genesis nor Imagex was immediately available for comment on Sunday.
In mid-October, Genesis had said he believed it had acquired 66 percent of Imagex's stock it had targeted in a conversion offer.

"Because of the severe financial condition and other activities which have occurred within Imagex's upper management, Genesis may elect to temporarily place Imagex into reorganization (Chapter 11) rather than a full-fledged bankruptcy liquidation in order to satisfy all creditors under court supervision while providing a green light for Genesis to introduce its capitalization and financial support without the threat of unfair financial burden created by what may be later deemed as gross negligence at best or criminal diversion and dilution of corporate assets for personal enrichment at its worst at the upper management levels of both current and former Imagex management," Genesis alleged in a statement.
The company said it may turn over information to the U.S. Department of Justice and the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
Genesis said it continues to believe Imagex is an "excellent turnaround target" that will not have a detrimental effect on Genesis' results.
Genesis said it intends to continue negotiating equipment leases and working with Imagex's creditors.
